events.title: Native Americans Granted U.S. Citizenship
events.description: President Calvin Coolidge signed the Indian Citizenship Act. It recognized as U.S. citizens all Native Americans born within the country's borders.
events.significance: The law extended citizenship to people whose nations were here long before the United States existed. Some states, however, kept denying Native Americans the vote for decades.

events.title: Italy Becomes a Republic
events.description: In a national referendum, Italians narrowly voted to abolish the monarchy and establish a republic. Women voted in a national election in Italy for the first time.
events.significance: The vote ended the House of Savoy's rule and began the modern Italian Republic. The date is still celebrated as Republic Day.

events.title: Elizabeth II Is Crowned
events.description: Elizabeth II was crowned at Westminster Abbey in London in a ceremony watched by millions around the world.
events.significance: It was the first major international event to be televised. It brought a coronation into ordinary living rooms for the first time.

events.title: Pope John Paul II Visits Communist Poland
events.description: Pope John Paul II arrived in Warsaw to begin a nine-day pilgrimage to his homeland. Huge crowds filled the streets to greet him. He was the first pope to visit a communist country.
events.significance: The visit energized Polish national and religious identity. Many historians see it as a spark for the Solidarity movement and the eventual fall of communism in Europe.
